import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_77/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_77/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_77/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source1 and Source2 on Source1.name == Source2.school
# This produces intermediate_step1 schema and data
step1 = pd.merge(
    source1,
    source2,
    left_on="name",
    right_on="school",
    how="inner",
    validate="one_to_one"
)
# Drop the redundant 'school' column from source2 after join
step1.drop(columns=["school"], inplace=True)

# Step 2: Join Source0 and Source1 on Source0.school == Source1.name
# This produces intermediate_step2 schema and data
step2 = pd.merge(
    source0,
    source1,
    left_on="school",
    right_on="name",
    how="inner",
    suffixes=("_student", "_school"),
    validate="many_to_one"
)

# Now, to produce the final Target4_77 table, we need to combine the aggregated scores and passing counts from step1
# with the school info from step1 (which has the scores) and the school IDs from step1.
# The target schema columns are:
# ['School ID': int, 'name': str, 'type': str, 'size': int, 'budget': int,
#  'Average Math Score': float, 'Average Reading Score': float,
#  'Number Passing Math': int, 'Number Passing Reading': int]

# The step1 dataframe already has all these columns except 'school' (which was dropped).
# So step1 is basically the target table except for the index and column order.

# We will reorder columns and ensure types match target schema.

# Reorder columns to target schema order
target_cols = [
    "School ID",
    "name",
    "type",
    "size",
    "budget",
    "Average Math Score",
    "Average Reading Score",
    "Number Passing Math",
    "Number Passing Reading"
]

target_df = step1[target_cols].copy()

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
target_df["School ID"] = target_df["School ID"].astype(int)
target_df["name"] = target_df["name"].astype(str)
target_df["type"] = target_df["type"].astype(str)
target_df["size"] = target_df["size"].astype(int)
target_df["budget"] = target_df["budget"].astype(int)
target_df["Average Math Score"] = target_df["Average Math Score"].astype(float)
target_df["Average Reading Score"] = target_df["Average Reading Score"].astype(float)
target_df["Number Passing Math"] = target_df["Number Passing Math"].astype(int)
target_df["Number Passing Reading"] = target_df["Number Passing Reading"].astype(int)

# Write the final target table to the specified path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source4_77_1 and Source4_77_2 on name=school
df_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")
df_1_2.drop(columns=["school"], inplace=True)

# Join the above result with Source4_77_0 on name=school
df_all = pd.merge(df_1_2, source0, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")
df_all.drop(columns=["school"], inplace=True)

# Group by the primary key columns of the target: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# Aggregate as per target schema:
# Average Math Score and Average Reading Score: average (mean)
# Number Passing Math and Number Passing Reading: sum
group_cols = ["School ID", "name", "type", "size", "budget"]

result = df_all.groupby(group_cols).agg({
    "Average Math Score": "mean",
    "Average Reading Score": "mean",
    "Number Passing Math": "sum",
    "Number Passing Reading": "sum"
}).reset_index()

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[[
    "School ID", "name", "type", "size", "budget",
    "Average Math Score", "Average Reading Score",
    "Number Passing Math", "Number Passing Reading"
]]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_77/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
